headline: An MIT Technology Review commentary argues that people's dislike of AI is aimed at the companies pushing it, even as use of AI keeps rising.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a commentary resting on published polls; its explanation is opinion, not new reporting.
importance_line: It frames the gap between public mistrust and daily use of AI as a reaction to company behaviour, which matters first to users, then to lawmakers, then to AI companies, but it is the author's opinion and the polls measure attitudes, not behaviour.
summary: In a commentary, MIT Technology Review notes that opinion is souring (Gallup found in May that 71% of US adults would oppose a new AI data centre nearby) while use keeps rising (Sensor Tower counted a billion monthly ChatGPT users in May), and argues that people dislike the companies' push of AI, not the technology. It adds that, unlike with social media, the public may still have some influence, since all 50 US states have passed or proposed AI laws, but concedes that trillion-dollar companies are hard to move.
notes: Read in full. First-person commentary; the poll figures are relayed from Gallup, Pew, Stanford, NBC and Sensor Tower as the article states them.
